label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.73), depression scores (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.73), and anxiety scores (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.13) are all in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring psychological distress. With 184 respondents in this cluster, it is a sizable group characterized by the convergence of heavy digital engagement and mental health challenges.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurring depressive and anxiety symptoms at above-average levels
High educational attainment paired with persistent emotional distress
Anxiety symptoms are the most pronounced of the three distress indicators
tone: Concerned and empathetic, grounded in empirical observation
